body:
### Summary

If no virtual environment exists, uv sync automatically creates the project's virtual environment (typically .venv) and then installs/synchronizes all dependencies specified in pyproject.toml and the lockfile into it.

The command `uv venv` supports the `--relocatable` flag and `UV_VENV_RELOCATABLE` envvar to make the virtual environment relocatable: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-venv--relocatable

This feature request proposes to support both the `--relocatable` flag and the `UV_VENV_RELOCATABLE` environment variable for `uv sync` with identical semantics to `uv venv` if not virtual environment exists.

### Example

Case 1: No virtual environment exists:

`uv sync --relocatable` is a shortcut for `uv venv --relocatable && uv sync`, both paths shall yield identical results

Case 2: A virtual environment exists:

This case needs design. `uv sync --relocatable` could either raise a warning about the flag being not supported for this case or reinstall all scripts to ensure the expected behavior of relocatable virtual environments.
title: Support --relocatable and UV_VENV_RELOCATABLE with uv sync
